title: 0342-blurball-joint-ball-and-motion-blur
universal_lens: The joint estimation of a dynamic object's midpoint and its instantaneous motion-blur vector forms a geometric isomorphism to recovering the first-order derivative of a trajectory from integrated exposure. This unifies discrete localization with continuous kinematic state, transforming blurred streaks into rigorous phase-space constraints.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps the blur vector as an auxiliary observation in a Bayesian filtering framework. The orientation and half-length provide a likelihood function for the velocity state, reducing posterior variance during high-speed transitions where standard point-mass tracking suffers from severe measurement noise.
gse_mapping: In GSE, the blur vector acts as a real-time differentiator for state transitions. By detecting discontinuities in the blur direction, the engine identifies bounce or deflection events, triggering piecewise quadratic trajectory fitting to maintain precise situational awareness during complex ball-flight dynamics.

primitives.name: Midpoint-Blur Vector Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Label schema: ball midpoint \(p_b\), blur orientation θ, blur half-length l; streak endpoints \(p_{1,2}=p_b\pm(l\cos\theta, l\sin\theta)\).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: p_b: Ball midpoint position (pixels); \theta: Blur orientation angle (degrees); l: Blur half-length (pixels); p_{1,2}: Streak endpoints (pixels).
primitives.assumptions: Motion blur is locally straight within a single camera exposure; the semantic center of the object corresponds exactly to the geometric midpoint of the blur streak.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails at bounce/impact events where the physical trajectory curves significantly within one exposure time, violating the linear streak assumption.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSE's upstream perception layer by converting raw pixel integration into explicit kinematic vectors, bypassing traditional finite-difference velocity estimators.
layer2.telemetry: Angle MAE (degrees) and length MAE (pixels) against manual segmentation.

primitives.name: PCA Blob Estimator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Detector: WASB (HRNet backbone) with squeeze-and-excitation attention; the heatmap is trained to cover the full line blur; quality focal loss; at inference, PCA of the thresholded blob estimates the blur angle θ and the projected extent estimates the half-length l.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \theta: Estimated blur angle (degrees); l: Estimated half-length (pixels); Heatmap: Probability density over spatial domain (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: The thresholded detection heatmap accurately preserves the elongated geometry of the underlying physical blur; the dominant principal component aligns with the true motion vector.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Suffers from high variance when blur is short (low signal-to-noise ratio), leading to unstable eigenvalue decomposition and unreliable angle extraction.

layer2.mapping: Functions as the perceptual kernel for GSI's conformal inference, providing the raw directional priors required to bound uncertainty sets during rapid object displacement.
layer2.telemetry: Detection F1 score and AP under varying blur ratios.

primitives.name: Discontinuity Bounce Detector
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Verdict:** ADAPT — the midpoint-plus-blur-vector label and blur-aware trajectory fitting are directly portable to NFL ball tracking (passes, punts, kicks), but the table-tennis detector and straight-blur assumption must be rebuilt for football geometry and broadcast cameras.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \Delta \theta: Change in blur orientation between consecutive frames (degrees); t: Time step (seconds).
primitives.assumptions: A sudden, non-smooth change in the estimated blur vector orientation signifies a physical interaction (e.g., bounce, tip, or catch) rather than sensor noise.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down under heavy occlusion or when broadcast camera jitter introduces artificial angular shifts that mimic physical deflections.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's event-trigger mechanism; replaces heuristic acceleration thresholds with direct optical flow derivatives to segment flight phases.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage reduction in trajectory fitting error on segmented bounces.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core mathematical innovation of BlurBall lies in elevating the motion blur from a nuisance artifact to a primary observable. Standard tracking relies on discrete point detections $p_t$, estimating velocity via finite differences $v \approx (p_{t+1} - p_t)/\Delta t$. This fails under high acceleration or low frame rates. BlurBall instead models the camera exposure as an integral operator $I(x) = \int_0^{T_{exp}} \delta(x - r(t)) dt$. Assuming locally linear motion $r(t) \approx p_b + v t$, the resulting image is a line segment centered at $p_b$ with length proportional to $|v| T_{exp}$ and orientation aligned with $v$. By jointly estimating $p_b$, $\theta$, and $l$, we recover the instantaneous velocity vector directly from a single frame, bypassing temporal differencing errors. The PCA estimator extracts these parameters from the thresholded heatmap blob, treating the dominant eigenvector as the motion axis. However, this linear approximation breaks down at impact events (bounces, tips), where curvature $r''(t)$ becomes significant within $T_{exp}$, causing the streak to bend or smear. The proposed adaptation for GSE leverages this breakdown: instead of discarding curved blurs, we detect the discontinuity in $\theta$ across frames to pinpoint the exact moment of impact. This allows us to fit piecewise quadratic trajectories, drastically improving air-distance and completion-probability models. The epistemic gain is substantial: we transform ambiguous, smeared pixels into rigorous kinematic constraints, provided the angle MAE remains below the critical threshold of 15 degrees.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive traces back to early cinematography analysis, where motion trails were used to estimate projectile speeds before digital tracking. Mathematically, it connects to the Radon transform and tomographic reconstruction, where line integrals reveal underlying structures. In computer vision, it parallels optical flow methods but operates at the exposure level rather than the pixel-displacement level, offering a more robust prior for high-speed dynamics.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a decision-theoretic perspective, the quarterback (or kicker) aims to maximize the receiver's catch probability by manipulating the ball's trajectory and spin. The defense attempts to disrupt this by introducing perturbations (hits, tips). BlurBall's discontinuity detector acts as an omniscient referee, instantly identifying when the ball's intended parabolic path is violated by an external force. This allows GSE to update the 'intent' model in real-time, distinguishing between a natural wobble and a tipped pass, thereby refining the expected points calculation.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: We must veto the direct application of the straight-blur assumption if the angle MAE variance exceeds 15 degrees on the target NFL dataset, as this indicates the PCA estimator is dominated by noise rather than signal. Furthermore, if the trajectory gain from incorporating blur vectors is less than 25% compared to a standard Kalman filter on point detections, the added complexity is unjustified. Finally, any leakage from manually segmented training trajectories into the test set must be strictly prevented to avoid inflated performance metrics.
